prompt: A hand-painted map of a whole continent seen from directly above, in the manner of a painted fantasy map such as a map of Middle-earth: coastlines, mountain ranges drawn as shaded ridges, rivers as fine dark lines running downhill to the sea, forests as textured masses, marsh, desert and open plain each in its own tone. Oil on parchment in a 19th-century academic manner with a smooth, finely blended surface, soft glazed transitions, fine detail, no heavy impasto. Palette of umber, ochre, gold, olive and sea-green with near-black shading. Less detail at larger scale; nothing drawn smaller than a hill or a wood; no settlements, no roads, no figures, no borders between countries. No text, no lettering, no compass rose, no scale bar, no frame, no grid, not photographic. The whole sheet is land and sea; nothing is cut off at the edges. One single continent fills most of the sheet, north at the top, with a margin of sea on every side so that no coast is cut off. The land is one broad mass, wider than it is tall, about four fifths of the sheet across and about three fifths of the sheet tall, about 1,100 miles east to west and 850 miles north to south, nowhere pinched narrower than half its width, with an irregular coast. A cold grey sea lies along the whole north. In the south-west one deep sheltered gulf bites into the land from the south-west coast toward the north-east, about a quarter of the land's width long and a tenth of it wide, about 250 miles long and 120 miles wide, with a mouth narrower than its body. The east and south coasts face open sea. The north-west quarter of the land is a broad highland of broken ridges cut by deep gorges and passes, not a single wall. Down the middle-east of the land, about two thirds of the way from the west coast to the east coast, runs a broken spine of hills and low mountains from near the north-east coast south to the hills behind the south coast, with gaps in it. The north coast at its middle is a broken rocky shore of small coves, headlands and scattered skerries, with bare hills behind it. The west of the land is flat lowland with one great dark forest and marsh along a slow river. In the exact middle of the sheet lies one round bare upland heath, pale and treeless, about forty miles across, a small pale disc about one twenty-fifth of the land's width, with open rolling plain all around it. West of the middle, between the heath and the gulf, a broad settled river plain in gold and green. East of the spine, wooded uplands on its eastern face fall to broad pale grazing plains that reach the east coast. In the south, river country of dark soil with stony hills behind it. East of the gulf, low brown hills. In the south-east, low green hills fall to a wide braided lowland of many channels and reed marsh. Rivers, each a fine dark line running downhill to a coast: one river in gorges from the north-west highland north to the cold sea; one slow winding river from the western foot of the highland west through the forest and marsh to the west coast; one long river from the southern face of the north-west highland south-east and then south across the western plain to the head of the gulf; one river from the plain south-west of the central heath south-west to the head of the gulf; one river from the low hills east of the gulf west to the head of the gulf; these three rivers part into many channels and meet at the head of the gulf in one wide delta of reed islands, with pale white salt flats on the delta's seaward side; one river from the south end of the spine south to the south coast, with one wide bend under stony hills; one river from the low hills of the south-east south-east through the braided lowland to a wide delta on the south-east coast; two short rivers from the eastern face of the spine east across the grazing plains, joining before the east coast; one river from the north end of the spine north-east to the north-east coast, with one great slow bend and reed marsh along its lower course.
